Pain conditions

Twelve reasons people come to Halcyon. One method for finding which is yours.

Wherever the pain starts, the plan is the same — find the structure generating it first, treat it second. Everything below is done without surgery, under local anaesthetic, as day care.

  • Ultrasound-guided
  • No general anaesthesia
  • Home the same day

Every condition treated at Halcyon, and what is usually done about it.

  • Knee Pain

    Osteoarthritis, meniscal tears and ligament pain

    The commonest reason people come to Halcyon. Depending on what the scan shows, the answer may be cooled radiofrequency of the genicular nerves, a regenerative injection, or prolotherapy. Advanced grade 4 arthritis with joint deformity is the one case where a replacement is still the right answer — and you will be told that plainly.

    COOLIEF cooled RF

    Read the full guide to knee pain

  • Low Back Pain

    Facet joint, disc and sacroiliac pain

    Low back pain can come from the facet joints, a disc or the sacroiliac joint, and those need different treatments. A diagnostic block is usually done first to prove which one it is, and the treatment follows from that.

    Diagnostic block first

    Read the full guide to low back pain

  • Neck Pain

    Facet joint, disc and muscular neck pain

    Neck pain is usually facet joint or disc related. A medial branch block identifies the joint involved, and cervical facet radiofrequency treats it if the block confirms the source.

    Medial branch block

    Read the full guide to neck pain

  • Shoulder Pain

    Frozen shoulder and rotator cuff injury

    Frozen shoulder and rotator cuff problems are treated with a suprascapular nerve block, hydrodilatation or a regenerative injection, depending on what the ultrasound shows — usually alongside a movement programme, so the range comes back.

    Suprascapular block

    Read the full guide to shoulder pain

  • Sciatica

    Leg pain radiating from a compressed nerve root

    Pain running from the back into the leg usually means a nerve root is being compressed. Treatment is a transforaminal or epidural injection placed under imaging, aimed at the root that is actually irritated rather than at the whole area.

    Transforaminal block

    Read the full guide to sciatica

  • Slipped Disc

    A herniated disc pressing on a nerve root

    In most cases a herniated disc is treated with an image-guided epidural injection rather than surgery. The scan and a diagnostic block confirm which level is involved before anything is done.

    Epidural injection

    Read the full guide to slipped disc

  • Hip Pain

    Bursitis, labral tears and an arthritic hip

    Hip pain from bursitis, a labral tear or an arthritic joint is treated with an image-guided injection into the exact structure involved. The hip sits deep enough that guidance matters more here than almost anywhere else.

    Image-guided injection

    Read the full guide to hip pain

  • Sports Injuries

    Tendon, ligament and overuse injury

    The injury is scanned to grade the damage, then treated with regenerative therapy or prolotherapy so the tissue heals rather than just quietens down. Return-to-sport timing is planned with you rather than handed to you.

    Regenerative therapy

    Read the full guide to sports injuries

  • Trigeminal Neuralgia

    Sudden electric pain across one side of the face

    When medication no longer controls the pain, radiofrequency ablation of the affected branch offers lasting relief. It is worth being assessed early — trigeminal neuralgia rarely settles on its own.

    Radiofrequency ablation

    Read the full guide to trigeminal neuralgia

  • Elbow, Hand & Wrist

    Tennis elbow, carpal tunnel and de Quervain’s

    Usually treated with nerve hydrodissection or a regenerative injection — freeing or repairing the structure rather than releasing it surgically. Ultrasound-guided fluid separates a trapped nerve from the tissue pressing on it, and the nerve itself is left intact.

    Nerve hydrodissection

    Read the full guide to elbow, hand & wrist

  • Foot & Ankle Pain

    Plantar fasciitis and Achilles tendinitis

    Heel pain that is worst on the first steps of the morning is usually plantar fasciitis; pain behind the ankle is often Achilles tendinitis. Both respond to prolotherapy or a regenerative injection placed under ultrasound.

    Prolotherapy

    Read the full guide to foot & ankle pain

  • Cervical Spondylosis

    Age-related wear through the cervical spine

    The wear itself shows on almost every scan after a certain age, so the scan alone does not make the diagnosis. A medial branch block is used to prove that the worn facet joints are what is actually hurting, and cervical facet radiofrequency treats them if it does.

    Cervical facet RF

    Read the full guide to cervical spondylosis

Nothing under that heading — try another part of the body.

Two people with the same X-ray do not always need the same procedure.

01

The examination narrows it

The consultant works out which structure is likely to be generating the pain — which is often not the place you feel it. Referred pain from the back to the leg, or from the neck to the arm, is the rule rather than the exception.

02

The ultrasound confirms it

The suspected joint, tendon or nerve is scanned in the same room. The scan is used twice: first to find the pain generator, then to guide the needle exactly where it needs to go.

03

A diagnostic block proves it

Where several structures could explain the same pain — the low back especially — a small diagnostic block is done first to prove which one it is. The treatment then follows from that answer, not from a guess.

Do not wait for an appointment

Sudden weakness in a limb, loss of bladder or bowel control, or back pain with fever needs to be seen urgently — go to a hospital emergency department now rather than booking a slot here. If you are not sure, call +91 77880 91092 and ask.

Not sure which one is yours?

That is what the first appointment is for. Bring any recent X-ray, MRI or scan reports — they often save a second visit.
